propositions: Multiple CI lanes lack per-test hang guards, allowing deadlocked tests to hide behind job-level timeouts with no traceback or culprit identification
Eight pytest-invoking CI lanes across five workflows need calibrated per-test timeout budgets based on historical runtime data with --timeout-method=thread to catch C-level blocking
The parity detection rule must distinguish pytest commands from non-invocations (pip installs, comments, arguments) using command-boundary matching across four invocation forms

Per-test budgets are calibrated at minimum 10x the lane's observed mean per-test duration (floored at 300s), with three exceptions: unexecuted test.yml external lane (600s), structured-output sweep (3600s for human-dispatched runs), and jira-dc-harness (900s to clear field-readiness waits)
_optionality.yml's degradation-path clean venv must install pytest-timeout alongside pytest and jsonschema to honor the timeout flags in its minimal environment

The extended parity assertion in test_ci_workflow_parity.py must cover all workflow files exhaustively and fail if any surviving pytest command line lacks both --timeout and --timeout-method=thread flags
